title: New photos show final moments of Vegreville standoff
article: New photos were released Wednesday showing the final moments of a fatal weekend standoff between RCMP and a 59-year-old man in Vegreville, Alta., 100 kilometres east of Edmonton.
Leo Raymond Poulin, 59, was shot three times in the chest Saturday evening by police in a Vegreville parking lot after he ignored their orders to put down a loaded shotgun.
The photos were taken by Don Yaremko from the Vegreville News Advertiser.
In one photo, Poulin is shown turning away from a police officer, presumably after being shot.
In the others, Poulin falls to the ground. The last photo shows an RCMP officer crouching over him, checking his pulse.
The shooting is under investigation by the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team, an independent agency that investigates incidents involving police that result in death or injury.

ASIRT director Clifton Purvis said Monday that Poulin's wife had called police telling them her husband was agitated and headed to the Vegreville detachment. Purvis said Poulin had been depressed and had recently stopped taking his medication.
Witnesses to the shooting said Poulin ignored repeated warnings from police to drop his weapon.
Poulin had no criminal record, and had had no dealings with police, other than receiving a speeding ticket two weeks ago.
A family spokesperson told CBC News on Monday that Poulin's actions were out of character for him and that he was a very kind and helpful person when he was healthy.
Poulin was a retired oil and gas industry worker who had been experiencing health problems in recent months, the family member said.
